nodes.question: Can the source mug be identified and tracked in the edited image well enough to judge its position relative to the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if the source mug can be matched to an edited object using visible identity or continuity cues, and that same object's position relative to the headphones can be judged. Fail if clear evidence shows the source mug is absent or unchanged and no matching moved mug is present. Unknown if blur, occlusion, or ambiguity prevents reliable matching or position judgment. Do not count a different mug as the source mug merely because it is visible.
nodes.binding: Compare source and edited images. Anchor the target to the single blue mug left of the headphones in the source; inspect the blurred blue remnant and any edited mugs for evidence of continuity. Record which edited object, if any, matches the source mug and why. This is evidence availability, not fulfillment.

nodes.question: Did the source mug itself move toward or to the right of the headphones, and is the requested relation complete?
nodes.criteria: Compare the source-identified mug with its edited counterpart, not any other mug. Pass only when evidence identifies that same mug and shows it to the right of the headphones. Fail when the same mug is identifiable but is not to the right; explicitly report whether it moved toward the requested position (progress) or shows no movement toward it. Unknown when identity, movement, or relative position cannot be resolved. A different mug on the right does not establish completion or progress. For R1, complete only on a verified same-mug right-side relation; partial only on evidenced movement of that mug toward the right without completion; absent only with clear evidence of no requested progress; otherwise unknown.
nodes.binding: Use source and edited images and the source-mug identity/continuity evidence from s1. State which edited object is tracked and the visual basis for matching it. Compare its source and edited positions relative to the headphones; do not infer movement from the presence of other mugs.

nodes.question: Is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Apply the original rubric to R1 using only the saved support observations. Complete (yes) only if s1 and s2 establish that the source mug itself is identified in the edit and is visibly to the right of the headphones. Partial only if s2 records evidence that this same mug moved toward the requested position but is not yet to the right. Absent (no) only if the observations provide clear evidence that no requested movement progressed. Unknown if source-mug identity, movement, or position is unresolved, or if the observations do not establish progress or absence. A different mug's position, object presence, or unrelated edits cannot establish fulfillment.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

s2: The repeated unknowns are valid executions, not transport or schema failures, but the binding is too vague and does not operationalize the supplied s1 identity/continuity evidence. Make the node explicitly consume s1’s tracked-object evidence and compare source-to-edited visual features and relative positions, while distinguishing a blurred remnant from a confidently matched mug. Require an explicit progress finding: whether the same mug moved rightward toward the headphones even if it did not reach the right side; reserve unknown for genuinely unresolved identity or displacement, not merely because the edited mug looks different or other mugs are present. Here the source is a distinctive large light-blue mug left of the headphones; the edit shows a blue blurred shape at far left and multiple smaller mugs, so assess whether the shape/placement and scene continuity support partial movement, without treating another mug as the source or assuming the reference label proves it. Report the matching cues, displacement, and confidence separately so the aggregate can distinguish evidenced partial progress from unresolved evidence.
s1: The binding is too vague and does not direct the node to use its identity/continuity evidence to assess progress. Make it explicitly compare the source mug’s distinctive features and location with the edited scene, identify any plausible match without assuming either white mug is the source, and assess whether the same mug shows rightward displacement toward the headphones even if its identity or final position remains uncertain. The edited image has a blurred blue shape at the former location and two smaller pale mugs, so distinguish evidence of movement from a confident object match; report match cues, displacement, and confidence separately. Keep unknown for genuinely unresolved identity or displacement, not merely because appearance changed or multiple mugs are present. Do not use the partial reference label as proof. The traces are valid executions, not transport/schema failures.

However, s2’s criteria only say to report visible movement toward the target as progress; they do not require recording whether such movement occurred when the mug is not yet to the right. The support evidence is insufficient for the rubric’s partial-versus-no distinction.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The support checks do not preserve the requested relation and extent reliably. s2 treats movement “toward” the right as partial even though the instruction only requests the final relation “to the right”; movement toward it could be in an unrelated direction or leave the mug still left of the headphones. Conversely, s2’s fail condition (“did not move toward”) does not establish that no requested progress occurred, so it cannot support absence. The fulfillment readout inherits this unsupported partial/absent logic. Require evidence of movement toward the right-side relation for partial, and clear evidence of no such progress for absent; otherwise leave unresolved.
